draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kayamkulam! This was once the capital of the Kingdom of Onattukara, and it's an old maritime trading town almost halfway between Alappuzha and Kollam.
draft.hungryLine: Kayamkulam is known for good fish dishes, and for toddy from the village toddy shops.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Puthiyodom Sri Krishna Swamy Temple is a 6 min walk, the Town Mosque is about 9 min, and Krishnapuram Palace is out on the Oachira road.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Watch coir and other coconut products being made at one of the local farms.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Krishnapuram Palace was built in the 18th century by Travancore Maharaja Marthanda Varma, and now holds a museum on the kingdom.

spots.name: Town Mosque
spots.detail: 9 min walk · In the town centre

spots.name: Krishnapuram Palace
spots.detail: On the Oachira road · Travancore palace and museum

tips.title: Plan around festival season.
tips.body: Chettikulangara Kumbha Bharani falls in the Malayalam month of Kumbham, and the Oachira temple holds its Vrishchikam festival every year.

tips.title: Change trains here.
tips.body: Kayamkulam Junction splits three ways, toward Kollam, Alappuzha and Kottayam.

story.title: A trading port
story.body: Kayamkulam grew as an ancient maritime trading centre on the coast.

story.title: Capital of Onattukara
story.body: The town was the capital of the Kingdom of Onattukara, and it's still the region's largest town.

story.title: Travancore's palace
story.body: Maharaja Marthanda Varma built Krishnapuram Palace between Kayamkulam and Oachira.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Temples, a palace and a busy rail junction. Tell me where you ended up.
